questions.knowledge_point: Dividing Rational Expressions and Simplifying the Result by Factoring
questions.worked_solution:
To compute

$$
\frac{8n}{2n-6}÷\frac{4n}{10n-30},
$$

we just need to multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8n}{2n-6}÷\frac{4n}{10n-30} & = \\ \frac{8n}{2n-6}\cdot \frac{10n-30}{4n} & = \\ \frac{4n\cdot 2}{2n-6}\cdot \frac{5(2n-6)}{4n} & = \\ \frac{\cancel{4n}\cdot 2}{\cancel{2n-6}}\cdot \frac{5\cancel{(2n-6)}}{\cancel{4n}} & = \\ 2\cdot 5 & = \\ 10\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Dividing Rational Expressions with Multiple Common Factors
questions.worked_solution:
Since $\frac{2(k+2)}{121y}\cdot Y=\frac{4(k+2)^{2}}{11{y}^{3}},$ we have

$$
Y=\frac{4(k+2)^{2}}{11{y}^{3}}÷\frac{2(k+2)}{121y}.
$$

To compute this quotient, we just need to multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4(k+2)^{2}}{11{y}^{3}}÷\frac{2(k+2)}{121y} & = \\ \frac{4(k+2)^{2}}{11{y}^{3}}\cdot \frac{121y}{2(k+2)} & = \\ \frac{2\cdot 2(k+2)\cdot (k+2)}{11y\cdot {y}^{2}}\cdot \frac{11\cdot 11y}{2(k+2)} & = \\ \frac{2\cdot \cancel{2(k+2)}\cdot (k+2)}{\cancel{11y}\cdot {y}^{2}}\cdot \frac{11\cdot \cancel{11y}}{\cancel{2(k+2)}} & = \\ \frac{2(k+2)}{{y}^{2}}\cdot 11 & = \\ \frac{22(k+2)}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Dividing Rational Expressions with a Single Common Factor
questions.problem: What is the result of dividing $\frac{9}{{t}^{3}}$ by $\frac{2}{t}?$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute

$$
\frac{9}{{t}^{3}}÷\frac{2}{t},
$$

we just need to multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{{t}^{3}}÷\frac{2}{t} & = \\ \frac{9}{{t}^{3}}\cdot \frac{t}{2} & = \\ \frac{9t}{2{t}^{3}} & = \\ \frac{9\cancel{t}}{2{t}^{2}\cdot \cancel{t}} & = \\ \frac{9}{2{t}^{2}} & \end{aligned}
$$

Note that in the final step, we canceled out a common factor of $t$ in the numerator and denominator.

questions.knowledge_point: Dividing Rational Expressions with a Single Common Factor
questions.worked_solution:
To compute

$$
\frac{5}{h}÷\frac{10}{k},
$$

we just need to multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{h}÷\frac{10}{k} & = \\ \frac{5}{h}\cdot \frac{k}{10} & = \\ \frac{5k}{10h} & = \\ \frac{\cancel{5}\cdot k}{\cancel{5}\cdot 2h} & = \\ \frac{k}{2h} & \end{aligned}
$$

Note that in the final step, we canceled out a common factor of $5$ in the numerator and denominator.

questions.knowledge_point: Dividing Rational Expressions with Multiple Common Factors
questions.worked_solution:
To compute

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{2{y}^{2}z}÷\frac{7{x}^{2}}{6{z}^{3}},
$$

we just need to multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{2{y}^{2}z}÷\frac{7{x}^{2}}{6{z}^{3}} & = \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{2{y}^{2}z}\cdot \frac{6{z}^{3}}{7{x}^{2}} & = \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{{y}^{2}\cdot 2z}\cdot \frac{3\cdot 2z\cdot {z}^{2}}{7\cdot {x}^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\cancel{{x}^{2}}}{{y}^{2}\cdot \cancel{2z}}\cdot \frac{3\cdot \cancel{2z}\cdot {z}^{2}}{7\cdot \cancel{{x}^{2}}} & = \\ \frac{3{z}^{2}}{7{y}^{2}} & \end{aligned}
$$
